Brandon Fortie’s Motion for Leave to File Late-Filed Direct Testimony Before the State Office of

Administrative Hearings 2 (“Motions”). The Motions should be denied because (1) the late filing of

20, 2026) (hereinafter “E6 Motion”) (Item No. 4800).
        2

Travis & Jennifer Reppond filed late testimony and/or exhibits at various times between May 22,

2026 and May 27, 2026.

        III.      RESPONSE TO MOTIONS FOR LEAVE TO FILE LATE TESTIMONY

   A. Granting the Motions Would Prejudice the Parties and Violate 16 Tex. Admin. Code §
      22.225(a)(10)
       Under 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 22.225(a)(10), “[l]ate-filed testimony may be admitted into

evidence if the testimony is necessary for a full disclosure of the facts and admission of the testimony

into evidence would not be unduly prejudicial to the legal rights of any party.” E6 Link Intervenors

assert that “allowing the testimony will not unfairly prejudice any party” and that “the parties will

still have a meaningful opportunity to review the testimony and prepare any response or cross-

examination.” 10 This assertion is incorrect. Since Dr. Carpenter’s testimony was filed at 4:31 p.m.

on the same day that intervenor cross-rebuttal was due, intervenors’ opportunity to respond to Dr.

Carpenter’s testimony effectively passed on the same day his testimony was filed. Dr. Carpenter is

testifying on behalf of the E6 Link Intervenors as to his opinion that any “E6 route would expose a

greater number of individuals and families to the potential risks and concerns associated with

prolonged EMF exposure”. 11       Dr. Carpenter’s testimony is therefore prejudicial to all parties

supporting routes that use Link E6. Further, Dr. Carpenter’s testimony was filed three working days

before Applicants’ rebuttal testimony was due, effectively cutting Applicants’ rebuttal response time

from 10 working days to three working days.




       10
            E6 Motion at 4.
       11
            E6 Motion at 10.


ONCOR AND LCRA TSC’S RESPONSE TO MOTIONS FOR LEAVE TO FILE DIRECT TESTIMONY AND
EXHIBITS OUT OF TIME AND OBJECTIONS TO LATE-FILED DIRECT AND SUPPLEMENTAL TESTIMONY

                                              Page 3 of 8
        This same logic applies to the late-filed direct testimony of Mr. Fortie. Mr. Fortie filed his

testimony only two days before the deadline for cross-rebuttal testimony and the parties to this case

and Applicants were prejudiced due to the shortened timelines for review and response.

   B. The E6 Link Intervenors and Mr. Fortie Did Not Timely Indicate They Intended to Offer
      Late-Filed Testimony
       16 Tex. Admin. Code § 22.225 requires parties that intend to offer late-filed testimony into

evidence to inform the presiding officer of their intent at the earliest opportunity so that the presiding

officer is able to establish reasonable procedures and deadlines regarding such testimony. The E6

Link Intervenors did not comply with this requirement, even with the knowledge that the deadline for

intervenor testimony passed on May 13, 2026. Instead, they waited two days after officially retaining

Dr. Carpenter on May 18, 2026, to indicate to the parties and the ALJs their intent to file late testimony

on May 22, 2026—the day that cross-rebuttal testimony was due. Mr. Fortie provided no reason in

his motion for leave to late-file testimony other than that he was unaware he had the option to file a

motion requesting leave to file late testimony. The E6 Link Intervenors’ and Mr. Fortie’s actions

allowed no time for the ALJs to establish reasonable procedures and deadlines to respond to these

late-filed testimonies.

   C. Allowing these Late-Filed Testimonies Will Disrupt the Orderly Resolution of this
      Proceeding
       The Administrative Law Judges established the procedural schedule in SOAH Order No. 6 to

promote the efficient and fair resolution of this case on a compressed timeline. The ALJs have already

declined to extend multiple deadlines in this proceeding, including the deadline for cross-rebuttal

to deposition scheduling or related procedural matters.” 13 This concession undercuts their own claim

that their late testimony filing will not disrupt the proceeding. 14 If accommodations are necessary,

then by definition the late filing does alter the procedural schedule for this case to the detriment of

parties who complied with the ALJs’ Order.

                           IV.      OBJECTIONS TO LATE-FILED TESTIMONY

above in Section III apply to these late-filed testimonies and testimony exhibits. Further, none of the

aforementioned parties filed motions requesting admission of their untimely filings. Accordingly, the

Applicants request the exclusion of these filings.
